thread:
simon: quick sync — ran a mixed-model co-residency run overnight, results look... surprising.
anna: surprise good or surprise bad? :eyes:
mike: screenshots? link to profile?
simon: dropping a short summary: 3 small and 1 mid model on a single A100-40G, soft partitioning, slab allocator. p95 latency regressed on mid model +22% under load.
rachel: ugh. was kernel selection consistent across requests? we saw fallback to slower attn kernels earlier.
simon: yes — kernel_pref steering was *mostly* to triton-fused, but when sequence len spiked we saw fallback to generic kernel.
jen: can you paste the kernel decision log? also what about KV cache hit-rate during the run?
simon: here are the relevant lines from the debug dump:

```
[2026-02-14T02:12:05Z] req=0x7fa kernel=triton-fused chosen=true seq_len=256 kv_state=hit
[2026-02-14T02:12:06Z] req=0x8ab kernel=generic-mha chosen=false seq_len=2048 kv_state=miss
[2026-02-14T02:12:07Z] req=0x9cc kernel=triton-fused chosen=true seq_len=128 kv_state=hit
```

simon: overall KV hit-rate fell from ~78% to ~55% during the spike window.
anna: that drop explains some of it — bigger seq -> kv miss -> more memory churn -> allocator fragmentation?
mike: allocator metrics pls. slab fragmentation numbers?
simon: slab lanes showed 14% internal fragmentation, free list thrash increased by 3x when generic kernel started allocating temporary workspaces for large seq.
jen: did workspace sizing adapt? we have a dynamic workspace growth patch but it throttles to avoid OOM.
rachel: we need to separate two vectors: kernel fallback due to seq_len and batching heuristic that pushed small requests into batches with large-seq requests. both amplify memory pressure.
mike: thought: try kv-prefetch + soft-evict on low-priority models so mid model keeps KV cache hot.
anna: also consider temporary workspace pooling to reuse buffers across kernels. those generic kernels allocate many ephemeral buffers.
simon: ran a quick experiment in dev: enabling workspace_pooling reduced transient allocations by ~40% and restored kv hit to ~70% in a synthetic mixed workload. p95 improved from 42ms -> 28ms for mid model.
jen: great. what's the config you used? quick paste please.
simon: experiment config:

```
alloc:
  scheme: slab+pool
  workspace_pool_mb: 384
  max_workspace_grow: 256
batching:
  dynamic_max_batch_ms: 6
  seq_aware_pack: true
routing:
  kv_prefetch_priority: ["mid-model"]
kernel_hint: ["triton-fused","triton-opt","generic-mha"]
```

rachel: nice. seq_aware_pack true prevents tiny prompts joining huge seqs, right?
simon: yes — it splits by predicted token length bins so we avoid heterogeneous batches that blow up workspace sizing.
mike: did you test multi-model isolation with soft VRAM caps? e.g., enforce 60% reserved for mid model at peak.
simon: tried soft-cap via reservation policy: it reduced throughput of small models but stabilized latency for the mid model. however it increased overall cost because GPU wasn't packed as tightly.
anna: tradeoff: strict reservation -> predictable latency, lower utilization; soft reservation + aggressive prefetch/evict -> better utilization but complex heuristics.
jen: thought: can we combine soft caps with eviction scoring that prefers evicting buffers from background models and preserves KV slots for priority models?
rachel: yes, eviction scoring already has model_priority and last_access_time. we can add "kv_importance" and "workspace_temp_score" weights.
simon: on the topic of kernel selection: the fallback decision point is currently purely sequence-length threshold. maybe incorporate allocator pressure into the decision — prefer kernels that minimize temporary workspace when free_mem < X.
mike: agree. kernel selection cost model should include transient_alloc_bytes and expected KV churn.
anna: small patch proposal: when free_mem < 1GB and seq_len between 512-1024, prefer kernel with lower transient alloc even if slightly slower flops.
jen: can you prototype a scoring function? we need to avoid oscillation — add hysteresis.
simon: prototype attached in thread gist (internal) but quick pseudocode:

```
score_kernel(k) = alpha*latency_est(k, seq) + beta*transient_alloc(k)/free_mem - gamma*kv_reuse_bonus
choose argmin(score_kernel)
```

simon: with alpha=0.7 beta=0.25 gamma=0.05 and 2s smoothing, it removed the fallback storm in the dev run.
rachel: impressive. what's the perf delta?
simon: in that run: mid-model p95 from 42ms -> 30ms, kv hit stabilised at 76%, fragmentation down to 7%.
mike: sounds promising. next step: run canary in a dedicated bin with 25% traffic to ensure nothing else regresses.
anna: also add metrics: kernel_choice_histogram, transient_alloc_rate, kv_hit_by_model, slab_frag.
jen: I'll add dashboards and alerts for kv_hit < 60% or transient_alloc_rate spike > 2x baseline.
simon: final note: swap strategy — we saw swap-to-host thrashing when eviction policy collided with kernel temp allocs. we should avoid swap churn by preemptively reclaiming lower-value caches before large-kernel allocations.
rachel: agree, implement prealloc guard: if we predict a large-kernel allocation > X, try to free up Y by evicting low-priority kv and reusing pool before letting kernel allocate.
mike: ok let's create two PRs: (1) kernel scoring + hysteresis, (2) workspace pooling + prealloc guard + eviction-weight tweaks.
jen: i'll own dashboards and canary rollout. tagging infra-bot to schedule canary window.
infra-bot: scheduled canary for 2026-02-16 03:00 UTC, duration 4h, route 25% traffic to canary pool.
simon: thanks team — will open PRs and post links here. keeping the plan small so we can iterate.
anna: :thumbsup:
